theory.intro: When $X$ is replaced by $aX+b$, the mean changes in the same way: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$. The spread ignores the shift, because $\mathrm{Var}(aX+b)=a^{2}\mathrm{Var}(X)$.
facts: $E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b$: multiply the mean by $a$, then add $b$.
$\mathrm{Var}(aX+b)=a^{2}\mathrm{Var}(X)$: the constant $b$ has no effect on the variance.
Adding $b$ shifts every value equally, so it moves the centre but leaves the distances between values unchanged.
The multiplier is **squared** in the variance because variance is built from squared deviations.
$\sigma(aX+b)=|a|\,\sigma(X)$, since the standard deviation is the square root of the variance.
These rules need only $E(X)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)$, not the whole distribution.
steps: Write the new variable in the form $aX+b$ and read off $a$ and $b$.

foundation.question_text: A random variable has $E(X)=4$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=3$. Find $E(2X+7)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(2X+7)$.
Raw test marks $X$ have mean $58$. The marks are scaled using $Y=1.2X+5$. Find the mean scaled mark.

development.question_text: A random variable has $E(X)=5.4$ and $\sigma(X)=2$. Find $E(10-4X)$ and $\sigma(10-4X)$.
The daily maximum temperature $X$, in degrees Celsius, has $E(X)=21.5$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=6$. The temperature in degrees Fahrenheit is $F=1.8X+32$. Find $E(F)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(F)$.
A random variable has $E(X)=8$, and $E(aX+5)=29$. Find $a$.
A random variable has $\mathrm{Var}(X)=2$, and $\mathrm{Var}(kX-7)=50$ where $k>0$. Find $k$.
A worker's weekly overtime hours $H$ have $E(H)=4.2$ and $\mathrm{Var}(H)=1.6$. Weekly pay in dollars is $W=920+45H$. Find $E(W)$ and $\sigma(W)$, correct to the nearest cent.

mastery.question_text:
The random variable $X$ has the distribution below.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc} x & 1 & 2 & 4 \\ \hline P(X=x) & 0.3 & 0.5 & 0.2 \end{array}$
Find $E(3X-5)$ and $\mathrm{Var}(3X-5)$.
A random variable has $E(X)=6$ and $\mathrm{Var}(X)=4$. The variable $Y=aX+b$ has $E(Y)=20$ and $\mathrm{Var}(Y)=36$, where $a>0$. Find $a$ and $b$.

A game's net gain $X$ in dollars has $E(X)=-0.5$ and $\sigma(X)=3$. The operator triples the player's net gain and then charges an extra $\$1$, so the new net gain is $Y=3X-1$. Find $E(Y)$ and $\sigma(Y)$, and state whether the change helps the player.
mastery.solution_text:
$E(Y)=3(-0.5)-1$
$=-1.5-1$
$=-\$2.50$
$\mathrm{Var}(X)=3^{2}$
$=9$
$\mathrm{Var}(Y)=3^{2}(9)$
$=81$
$\sigma(Y)=\sqrt{81}$
$=\$9$
The expected loss per play grows from $\$0.50$ to $\$2.50$ and the spread trebles, so the change does not help the player.
